# input-joystick

> A touch-anywhere floating virtual joystick for React canvas games: a component that claims one
> pointer inside a host element and emits normalized vectors, a pure deadzone/clamp function, an
> opt-in WASD/arrow-key co-map, a claim-area predicate for which presses the stick takes, and a
> pointer-ownership registry that arbitrates which subsystem owns a finger. It owns pointer claiming
> and hit-testing; the game owns what the vector means and how it looks.

## Docs

- [Documentation site](https://jbcom.github.io/input-joystick/): the published, browsable version
  of everything below.
- [README](https://github.com/jbcom/input-joystick/blob/main/README.md): install, quick start, API
  overview, behavior, compatibility.
- [API reference](https://github.com/jbcom/input-joystick/blob/main/docs/API.md): full signatures,
  defaults and pointer rules for every export.
- [Architecture](https://github.com/jbcom/input-joystick/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): module
  boundaries, invariants, intentional limits.
- [Decisions](https://github.com/jbcom/input-joystick/blob/main/docs/decisions.md): why the package
  and repository are shaped the way they are.
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/jbcom/input-joystick/blob/main/AGENTS.md): toolchain, invariants
  not to violate, and doc/test sync obligations for an autonomous coding agent.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/jbcom/input-joystick/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): local setup,
  the `pnpm verify` gate, commit and release conventions.
